Sovereignty by design

Data and agent processing that stays under Canadian control.

Agents are only as trustworthy as where they run and what they can see. We design residency, identity, and access before we write the first prompt.

Canadian regions first

Fabric capacities, storage, and agent services pinned to Canada Central and Canada East, with model availability confirmed per workload.

Identity-bound agents

Agents inherit the signed-in user's Entra ID permissions and use managed identities. No shared keys, no over-broad service accounts.

Governed and labelled

Purview sensitivity labels, DLP, and lineage follow data from OneLake into every agent response.

Monitored and defended

Defender and Azure logging watch agent traffic, with prompt-injection and data-leak testing before go-live.

Private by default

Private endpoints, managed networks, and customer-managed keys where your policy calls for them.

Your data is not training data

Azure AI Foundry services process your prompts and data in your tenant; they are not used to train the underlying models.

Read the sovereignty approach →
